summary: An announcement from Steve Bunch that the next Network Graphics Working Group meeting might be held at the University of Illinois on May 11, 1973, with a final date to follow. It also invites anyone with comments on higher-level graphics protocols to write them up as RFCs beforehand. It updates RFC 396.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 474 proposes a date and location for a Network Graphics Working Group meeting. It also asks people to send in their views on higher-level graphics protocols before the meeting.

sections.title: A Proposed Meeting in Illinois
sections.content:
Ira Cotton of NBS proposed that Illinois host the next Network Graphics Working Group meeting in early May. Steve Bunch asks whether there are pressing reasons not to hold it on Friday, May 11, 1973.

The note says a formal announcement of the final date and local arrangements would follow in a week or two. It does not confirm that the suggested date was adopted.
sections.plainLanguage: The group was considering a meeting in Illinois on May 11, 1973. The note asks people to raise serious objections before the final date is announced.

sections.title: How to Contact the Organizer
sections.content:
The note gives a mailing address at the Center for Advanced Computation, University of Illinois, Urbana, Illinois 61801. It also lists two telephone numbers and says Bunch could be reached through the network at BUNCH@USC-ISI.

These details are provided so readers can respond about the proposed meeting arrangements.
sections.plainLanguage: Readers could respond by mail, telephone or network message using the contact details in the notice.

sections.title: Call for Protocol Ideas
sections.content:
Bunch invites ideas, comments, suggestions and criticism about higher-level graphics protocols. He asks people to express their views in an RFC before the meeting, giving everyone time to consider them.

The unit metadata records that RFC 474 updates RFC 396.
sections.plainLanguage: People interested in graphics protocols are asked to write down their views before the meeting. That gives others time to read and consider them.
